word:lxx:L706745.explanation: This Greek LXX verb means “desire”: it expresses wanting or longing for something. word:lxx:L706792.explanation: Ira is a personal name, referring to an individual rather than expressing an action, quality, or general idea. word:lxx:L706851.explanation: Istōb, also rendered Istov, is a proper name in the Greek Old Testament. word:lxx:L706972.explanation: Kadēmōth, also rendered Kathimoth, is a proper name rather than a general word describing an action, quality, or object. word:lxx:L707096.explanation: This noun refers to the character and conduct of a person—the qualities shown in who someone is and how that person behaves. It brings inner character and outward conduct together as one subject. The word occurs five times in the Greek LXX corpus, all in 4 Maccabees. Its precise emphasis in any particular verse depends on the surrounding passage, but its basic sense concerns a person’s character expressed through conduct.

word:lxx:L707122.explanation: Kanaath is a proper name, referring to a particular person or place identified by that name rather than describing an action, quality, or relationship. The available lexical information preserves the name itself but does not provide enough surrounding verse text to explain further details about whom or what Kanaath identifies. Its precise significance in that passage therefore depends on reading the verse and its broader context.

word:lxx:L707157.explanation: Karmilia is a proper name, given in the gloss as “Karmēlia; Karmilia.” It identifies a named individual or designation rather than describing an action, quality, or object. In the Greek LXX corpus, this name occurs once, at 1 Chronicles 3:1. The available lexical information establishes the name’s identity and spelling, while the surrounding verse text would be needed to explain the person’s particular role in that passage.

word:lxx:L707328.explanation: This noun means “division into parts,” describing the separating or apportioning of something into distinct portions. In the Greek Old Testament, it appears once, in Joshua 13:14, so its normal sense is clear even though the surrounding verse text is not included here. The word points to an arrangement in which something is distributed by parts rather than treated as one undivided whole.

word:lxx:L707456.explanation: This Greek LXX verb means “rejoice”: to express gladness or delight. It describes an action rather than a person or object, so it tells what someone does when responding with joy. The word appears once in the Greek Old Testament represented here, in Zephaniah 3:14. Its basic meaning is clear from the direct definition and does not require adding a more specific emotional or spiritual idea without the surrounding verse and passage.

word:lxx:L707614.explanation: This Greek LXX verb means “hollow” or “hollow out.” It describes making something hollow, or expressing the condition of being hollow. The word appears twice in the Greek LXX, both times in Jeremiah: Jeremiah 14:2 and Jeremiah 15:9. These occurrences belong to the Old Testament Greek corpus, and the word’s precise force in either verse depends on the surrounding passage. Its basic idea remains the removal of what fills or supports the inside, leaving something hollow.

word:lxx:L707760.explanation: This Greek LXX word is a proper name, given as “Koilē; Kili.” It functions as a name rather than expressing an action, quality, or general concept. Its exact referent must be determined from the surrounding verse, since the lexical information identifies the name but does not provide the verse text. The word occurs seven times in the Greek LXX corpus, appearing in Leviticus and 1–2 Maccabees.

word:lxx:L707805.explanation: This verb means “obtain,” describing the act of coming into possession of something. It functions as an action word, not as the name of a person, object, or quality. In the Greek Old Testament and related Greek Jewish writings represented in this corpus, it occurs 20 times, showing use across multiple passages rather than only one setting. Its precise force in a particular verse depends on what is being obtained and the surrounding sentence. It appears in texts ranging from Genesis through 4 Maccabees.

word:lxx:L707849.explanation: This adjective describes something that fills the world or is worldwide in reach. It points to broad extent rather than a local or limited scope, expressing a presence that spreads throughout the inhabited world. The word occurs once in the Greek LXX corpus, in 4 Maccabees 15:31. Its precise force in that verse depends on the surrounding passage, but its central sense is something world-filling or worldwide.

word:lxx:L708093.explanation: This noun refers to an “enrolment” or “census,” meaning a formal registering or counting of people. It names the act or record of listing a population, rather than describing an individual person. In the Greek LXX corpus, it occurs once, in 3 Maccabees 2:28. Its precise force in that passage depends on the surrounding verse and context, but its basic meaning remains a population enrolment or census.

word:lxx:L708141.explanation: This adverb means “imperceptibly”: in a way that is not noticed or detected. It describes an action or change taking place without attracting attention, so readers understand that something happened quietly or beyond ordinary awareness. In the Greek LXX corpus represented here, it occurs twice, both times in 2 Maccabees. Its exact force in either passage depends on the surrounding verse, but its central meaning remains the same: something occurs without being perceived.

word:lxx:L708215.explanation: This Greek LXX verb means “oil” or “get rich.” It can describe applying oil, or becoming prosperous and well supplied. The word appears eight times in the Greek Old Testament and related deuterocanonical writings, so its exact sense depends on the sentence in which it occurs. Its basic idea is connected either with oil as a substance or with becoming enriched. In one recorded rendering, it is translated “oil.”

word:lxx:L708259.explanation: This Greek LXX noun means “mane,” the longer hair growing around an animal’s neck. It names a visible physical feature rather than an action or quality. Since those passages are boundary descriptions and the verse text is not included here, the word’s basic meaning is clear, while its exact reference in each description belongs to the surrounding passage.

word:lxx:L708390.explanation: This verb means “deliver”: to bring someone out of danger, difficulty, or an unwanted condition. In the Greek Old Testament, it occurs twice, in Exodus and Job, so its normal meaning is clear even though the surrounding verse text is not included here. The precise force in either passage depends on how the sentence uses the verb. Its basic idea remains the act of delivering or bringing someone out.

word:lxx:L708400.explanation: This word means “in a blessed way” or “blessed.” As an adverb, it describes how something is done or how someone is regarded, marking a condition of blessing or happiness rather than naming a person or object. In the Greek Old Testament corpus represented here, it appears once, in 4 Maccabees 12:1. The exact force of that occurrence depends on the surrounding verse and passage, which are not included here.

word:lxx:L708581.explanation: Matekka is a proper name: it identifies a named person or place rather than describing an action, quality, or general object. word:lxx:L708747.explanation: Merimōth, rendered Merimoth, is a proper name referring to a person. word:lxx:L708866.explanation: This word means “neither of the two.” It is an adjective used to describe two alternatives when both are excluded. This word should be kept distinct from Greek New Testament vocabulary because this entry belongs to the Greek Old Testament corpus.

word:lxx:L708938.explanation: This word means “hired,” describing a person who works for pay or something connected with being hired. The precise force in any particular verse depends on the surrounding sentence, but the central idea remains someone or something associated with being hired.

word:lxx:L708963.explanation: This noun refers to a memorial or tomb—a place connected with remembering and burying the dead. In the Greek Old Testament, it is used for burial places and the sites where the dead are laid to rest. Its basic sense remains a physical memorial or tomb, while the surrounding passage determines the particular emphasis. “Tomb” is also an attested English rendering.

word:lxx:L709076.explanation: This word is a proper name, rendered “Mysarchēs” or “Misarkhis,” rather than a common term describing an action, quality, or object. The available wording preserves the name in two transliterated forms but does not provide an additional descriptive meaning or explain the person’s role.

word:lxx:L709119.explanation: Naaliēl is a proper name, referring to a specific named entity rather than expressing a general idea or action. word:lxx:L709182.explanation: Nambra, also rendered Namvra, is a proper name rather than a word describing an action, quality, or object. It identifies a named subject in the Greek Old Testament text. This name occurs once in the Greek LXX, at Numbers 32:3. The available information establishes the name’s wording and use as a designation, but does not provide enough surrounding verse text to explain more specifically whom or what it identifies.

word:lxx:L709308.explanation: Nikanōr, also rendered Nikanor, is a personal name rather than a word describing an object, action, or quality. word:lxx:L709353.explanation: Noom is a personal name, rendered as “Noom.” It identifies an individual rather than describing an action, quality, object, or relationship. In the Greek Old Testament, this name occurs once, at 1 Chronicles 4:15. Because the available passage text is not included here, the name’s particular role in that verse cannot be described further. Its ordinary lexical function is simply to designate the person called Noom.

word:lxx:L709410.explanation: This noun refers to friendly gifts or tribute—something offered as a gesture of goodwill, honor, or acknowledgment. It appears once in the Greek Old Testament, in Ezra 1:6. The word therefore names an offering presented to another person rather than an action or quality. Its precise force in that verse depends on the surrounding passage, but its basic sense centers on gifts given in friendship or as tribute.

word:lxx:L709537.explanation: This noun refers to a “gadfly,” also called a “breese”—a flying insect known for harassing or stinging. It names the creature itself rather than an action or quality. In the Greek LXX corpus represented here, the word occurs twice, both times in 4 Maccabees, at 2:3 and 3:17. The surrounding verse text is needed to explain how the image functions in either passage; the word’s basic meaning remains the insect named by the gloss.

word:lxx:L709595.explanation: Holorrizi means with the entire root.

word:lxx:L709605.explanation: This word refers to a kind of grain, specifically spelt. It is a noun naming a cultivated cereal used among other grains. word:lxx:L709649.explanation: This Greek LXX verb means “produce sour grapes.” It describes the action of bringing forth grapes with a sour quality, rather than simply naming a grape. word:lxx:L709814.explanation: This Greek LXX adverb means “by no means.” It expresses a strong denial or rejection, indicating that something is not to be accepted or understood under any circumstance. Its exact force in a particular sentence comes from the surrounding context.

word:lxx:L709883.explanation: This word means “mob.” It is a verb describing the action of mobbing—people acting together as a crowd rather than as isolated individuals. In the Greek LXX, it appears once, so its normal sense is clear, but its precise force in 3 Maccabees 5:41 must be determined from that verse and its surrounding passage. It should be understood as an action word, not a name for a person or object.

word:lxx:L709960.explanation: This LXX adverb means “all the nation,” expressing something that applies to an entire people collectively rather than only to selected individuals. It describes the scope of an action, condition, or experience as reaching the nation as a whole. The word occurs once in the Greek text represented here, in Wisdom 19:8. Its precise force in that verse depends on the surrounding wording and passage, but its basic meaning emphasizes complete national scope.

word:lxx:L710074.explanation: This Greek LXX noun refers to consolation or encouragement—support that comforts and strengthens someone. The word occurs once in the Greek LXX corpus, in Wisdom 3:18, so its broader range must be understood from its basic meaning rather than from many examples. Its precise force in that verse depends on the surrounding passage.

word:lxx:L710140.explanation: This adjective means “incidental.” It describes something that accompanies the main matter without being its central focus. Its exact force in that verse depends on the surrounding wording, but its basic sense remains something incidental—present alongside the main matter rather than defining it.

word:lxx:L710225.explanation: This verb means “try” or “test”—to put someone or something through an experience that reveals what they will do or whether they are genuine. It occurs 45 times in the Greek Old Testament and related deuterocanonical books, from Genesis through 4 Maccabees. Its precise force in a particular passage depends on who is doing the testing and what is being tested.

word:lxx:L710269.explanation: This noun describes a person who is twenty-five years old. It identifies a specific age rather than an action, quality, or relationship. In the Greek Old Testament, it appears seven times, all in the book of Numbers, where it serves as an age designation. Its meaning is precise and straightforward: the person being described has reached twenty-five years of age. The word’s exact role in any particular verse depends on the surrounding sentence, but its basic meaning remains the same.

word:lxx:L710287.explanation: This LXX Greek verb means “head around” or “go around,” describing movement from one place or direction around another. word:lxx:L710423.explanation: This word means “surrounding territory”—the land or region around a particular place. In the Greek Old Testament, it appears 21 times, showing a repeated focus on geographical areas around cities, lands, or other locations. Its precise force in any verse depends on which place or region it describes, but its central idea remains the territory lying around something else.

word:lxx:L710517.explanation: This Greek LXX adverb means “more frequently” or “oftener.” It describes an action or event that happens with greater frequency than another, or happens repeatedly. It appears eight times in the Greek Old Testament and Greek deuterocanonical writings, including Psalms, Isaiah, Sirach, and Maccabees. Its precise force in any particular verse depends on what action or event the surrounding sentence compares or repeats.

word:lxx:L710724.explanation: This Greek verb means “make soft; mild.” It describes making something gentle, less harsh, or mild rather than hard or severe. As a verb, it points to an action or change, not merely a quality. In the Greek Old Testament, it occurs twice, in Psalms and Proverbs. Its exact sense in either passage depends on the surrounding verse, but its central idea remains the softening or mildening of something.

word:lxx:L710816.explanation: Prokyneō means to worship or bow down in reverence.

word:lxx:L710939.explanation: This verb means “lament at,” expressing sorrow directed toward a person, event, or situation. It describes an act of grieving or mourning in response to something. The word’s precise force in that passage depends on the surrounding verse and context, but its central sense is an expression of sorrow concerning something. word:lxx:L711028.explanation: This Greek LXX noun means “one who plays the first part” or “chief actor”—the leading person in an event, struggle, or public action. Its precise force in either passage depends on the surrounding context, but its central idea remains a person occupying the leading place.

word:lxx:L711073.explanation: This Greek LXX noun means “bankruptcy,” referring to a condition of financial collapse or inability to meet one’s obligations. Its exact force in any passage depends on the surrounding verse and whether the context emphasizes poverty, loss, or financial ruin.

word:lxx:L711257.explanation: Riba, also rendered Rhiva, is a proper name rather than a word describing an action, quality, or object. The name itself does not provide an additional definition or spiritual concept apart from identifying the person.

word:lxx:L711330.explanation: Saaria is a proper name, referring to a person named Saaria rather than describing an action, quality, or object. word:lxx:L711396.explanation: Salamanassar is a proper name, referring to a person named Salamanassar. In the Greek Old Testament, this name occurs once, in 2 Kings 18:9. word:lxx:L711460.explanation: Sameri is a personal name, referring to an individual rather than expressing an action, quality, or general idea. word:lxx:L711514.explanation: Sarath is a proper name, referring to a named place or person rather than expressing an action, quality, or general idea. word:lxx:L711756.explanation: This Greek LXX noun means “moth,” the small insect associated with damaging or consuming clothing and other materials. word:lxx:L712137.explanation: This Greek LXX verb means “squeeze out”: to press something so that its contents or liquid come out. It describes an action rather than a person, object, or quality. word:lxx:L712142.explanation: This noun means a strategem or trick: a deliberate tactic used to achieve an aim, often through cleverness or deception. word:lxx:L712195.explanation: This verb means “sit together”: to be seated with other people rather than alone. It describes shared sitting or occupying a place in company with others. word:lxx:L712205.explanation: This verb means to inherit with someone else—to receive a common inheritance together with another person. word:lxx:L712249.explanation: This noun means “husbands,” referring to men joined in marriage. word:lxx:L712476.explanation: This adjective means “put together” or “composite,” describing something formed from multiple parts joined into one. word:lxx:L712519.explanation: Syntribē means crushing. It can also mean breaking.

word:lxx:L712555.explanation: This word means “signal”: a visible or recognizable sign used to communicate a message, give notice, or direct attention. word:lxx:L712582.explanation: This word means “close” or “lock”. It is a verb for shutting something so that it is secured and does not remain open. word:lxx:L712601.explanation: This word refers to a figure or scheme: something understood as a recognizable form or plan.
